findings.evidence: The UI now schedules a timer for the next previewExpiresAt in the active preview or history, derives currentPreviewExpired from current time, displays EXPIRED, and hides confirm actions for active and historical previews after expiry.
findings.why_it_matters: After expiry, the UI can still label the preview ready and invite confirmation. The backend rejects the expired batch, protecting assignment integrity, but the Host sees stale status and may trigger an unnecessary failed action.
findings.required_action: Reconcile the active preview with the matching batch status returned by overview and/or refresh its state at previewExpiresAt. Once expired, show the batch-specific expiry message and hide or disable its confirmation action.

findings.evidence: The RANDOM confirm path compared the attempt-ID scope snapshot but did not compare the per-attempt eligible-answer counts captured in assignment entries. If answer eligibility changed without changing the attempt set, the batch could commit with an obsolete Examiner-load count.
findings.why_it_matters: Persisted per-Examiner answer counts would no longer describe the current eligible work shown by the preview, misleading Host load summaries.
findings.required_action: Compare each previewed per-attempt eligible-answer count with the current resolver result for both allocation modes and persist the preview as STALE when any count differs.

review_context: Verification of prior findings: QUAL-026 remains resolved by the expiry timer/status and hidden confirmation action; QUAL-027 remains resolved by comparing per-attempt eligible-answer counts before commit. The Jackson dependency alignment received runtime validation through a successful API startup and Host preview. The added database integration tests exercise concurrent confirm and repeated 40-attempt preview/commit through the real assignment service and H2 JPA repositories. Concurrent confirms serialize through the batch-row PESSIMISTIC_WRITE lock; the session-row lock facade and other module facades are mocked, so those behaviors and HTTP/PostgreSQL performance are not verified here. Latest run passed 2/2 tests and recorded 129 ms p95 across 20 measured runs (3 warmups), with exact 20/20 allocation. Plan/test prose states these boundaries and records that the seeded session was not committed. No open blocking findings remain.
